hook: Sharks are older than trees.
facts: The first sharks were already swimming about four hundred and fifty million years ago.
Trees came later, when plants finally learned how to grow tall and hard.
So sharks watched the first forest appear, and they are still here after it.

hook: Sloths hold their breath longer than dolphins.
facts: A dolphin has to come up for air after about ten minutes.
A sloth can slow its own heart down until it needs almost no air.
That way it stays under water for up to forty minutes, longer than any dolphin.

hook: Nintendo is older than sliced bread.
facts: The company started in Japan in eighteen eighty-nine, making paper playing cards by hand.
For about seventy years it sold cards, and it even tried taxis and instant rice.
So Nintendo made playing cards for longer than it has made video games.

hook: Saturn would float in water.
facts: Saturn is enormous, but it is mostly gas held together by its own weight.
For its size it is lighter than water, the only planet around our sun like this.
Find an ocean big enough and the whole planet would sit on top and bob.

hook: A tiny animal survived the vacuum of space.
facts: It is called a tardigrade, and it is smaller than a grain of salt.
Scientists left some outside a spacecraft, with no air, no water and no cover.
Most came back alive, and some even laid eggs that hatched normally afterwards.

hook: One jellyfish can turn back into a baby.
facts: It is a small jellyfish called Turritopsis, about as wide as your little fingernail.
When it is hurt or hungry, its body melts back into the young shape it started from.
Then it grows up all over again, and it can do this as often as it needs.

hook: One shrimp punches so fast the water boils.
facts: The mantis shrimp swings its front claw as fast as a bullet leaving a gun.
The claw moves so fast that the water in front of it tears open into a bubble.
For an instant that bubble gets thousands of degrees hot and gives off a flash of light.

hook: A whale tongue weighs as much as an elephant.
facts: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived on this planet.
Its tongue on its own can weigh around three thousand kilograms.
And its open mouth can hold about ninety thousand kilograms of water and food.

hook: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep.
facts: Otters sleep on their backs, floating on the top of the water.
The sea keeps moving all night, so a sleeping otter would drift away alone.
They hold paws in long lines called rafts, and the whole group wakes up together.

hook: Flamingos are not born pink.
facts: A baby flamingo comes out grey, and it looks nothing like its parents.
The pink comes from its food: small shrimp and algae full of natural color.
A flamingo that stops eating them turns pale again, like color washing out of a shirt.

hook: Peanuts are not nuts.
facts: A real nut grows on a tree, inside a hard shell, the way a walnut does.
Peanuts grow under the ground, in the soil, exactly like beans and peas.
So peanut butter is closer to a bowl of peas than to a bag of almonds.

hook: Bananas are berries, but strawberries are not.
facts: For scientists a berry is a fruit from one flower, with its seeds inside.
A banana follows that rule, so it counts as a berry, and so does a grape.
A strawberry grows from many flowers and carries its seeds outside, so it fails.

hook: There is a room too quiet for people.
facts: It is a laboratory in the United States, built to swallow almost every sound.
With no sound left around you, you start hearing the sounds inside your own body.
People hear their heart, their lungs and their blood, and few stay half an hour.

hook: The national animal of Scotland does not exist.
facts: Most countries choose a real animal, like an eagle, a lion or a bear.
Scotland chose the unicorn hundreds of years ago and never changed its mind.
It is still on the royal coat of arms today, and it is drawn wearing a gold chain.

hook: The dot on the letter i has a name.
facts: It is called a tittle, and the word is around seven hundred years old.
It was not there at first: writers added it so two letters would not blur together.
So the smallest mark you write every day has a name, and nobody ever uses it.

hook: Bees can remember a human face.
facts: Researchers showed bees photographs of people, with sugar next to one of the faces.
The bees learned which face meant food, and they came back to it days later.
They do not see a person: they read the pattern of your eyes, nose and mouth.

hook: On Mars, the sunset is blue.
facts: Here on Earth the air spreads blue light around the sky and leaves the sunset red.
The dust on Mars does the opposite: it keeps the red light and lets blue through.
So the sky there is dusty orange all day, and only the sunset goes blue.

hook: Astronauts come home taller than they left.
facts: On Earth, gravity presses the soft pads between the bones of your back all day.
In space nothing presses, so the spine stretches out and the whole body gets longer.
Astronauts can gain about five centimeters, and they lose it again back on the ground.

hook: The smell of rain has a name.
facts: It is called petrichor, and it is not the smell of water at all.
Dry soil holds oils from plants and tiny living things, and rain throws them into the air.
So what you smell is the ground itself, opening up after weeks of being shut.

hook: Cashews grow on the outside of a fruit.
facts: Each cashew hangs under a soft red fruit, one single nut for each fruit.
The shell around it holds an oil that burns skin, the same family as poison ivy.
That is why nobody sells cashews in the shell: someone has to roast them for you first.

hook: Carrots used to be purple.
facts: For hundreds of years carrots were purple, white or yellow, and nobody minded.
Dutch growers slowly bred the orange ones, and people liked the way they looked.
The orange carrot won so completely that a purple one now looks like the strange one.

hook: A koala could confuse a crime laboratory.
facts: Koalas have fingerprints, with loops and lines, which almost no other animal has.
Under a microscope they look so close to ours that experts can mix the two up.
So a koala print at a crime scene could be filed as a human one by mistake.

hook: One animal almost never gets cancer.
facts: It is the naked mole rat, a wrinkled animal that lives underground in Africa.
Its body makes a thick sugar between its cells that stops tumors from spreading.
It also lives about ten times longer than a mouse, and it barely looks older.

hook: Some frogs freeze solid every winter.
facts: The wood frog does not dig deep: it lets the cold take it, under the leaves.
Up to two thirds of the water in its body turns to ice, and its heart stops.
In spring it thaws, the heart starts again, and the frog hops away as if nothing happened.

hook: One animal can regrow part of its brain.
facts: The axolotl is a salamander from Mexico that never grows out of its baby shape.
Cut off a leg and it grows back, with bones, nerves and skin in the right places.
It can even rebuild parts of its heart and its brain, and it leaves no scar.

hook: Some bamboo grows a meter in a day.
facts: Bamboo is not a tree at all: it is a grass, and grass pushes up from the bottom.
The whole stem is already folded inside the shoot, so the plant only has to lift it.
The fastest kinds add almost one meter in a single day, and the stem creaks as it goes.

hook: Butterflies taste with their feet.
facts: A butterfly has tiny sensors on its legs that work like the tip of your tongue.
It lands on a leaf, tastes it through its feet, and knows if the plant is right.
That is how a mother picks where to lay her eggs, without ever taking a bite.

hook: A penguin proposes with a stone.
facts: Gentoo penguins build their nest out of pebbles, and good pebbles are hard to find.
A male searches the beach, picks the smoothest one, and drops it at her feet.
If she keeps the stone they build the nest together, and some pairs stay for years.

hook: Bananas are slightly radioactive.
facts: Bananas are full of potassium, and a small part of all potassium is radioactive.
It is so little that scientists joke about it, and use bananas to explain radiation.
You would have to eat millions of bananas in one day for it to hurt you.

hook: Honey found in a tomb was still edible.
facts: Archaeologists opened Egyptian tombs and found jars of honey thousands of years old.
Honey holds almost no water and is naturally acidic, so bacteria cannot live in it.
Sealed properly it never goes off, which almost no other food on your shelf can do.
